doc.title: Christian McBride interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996

title: Jazz in New York and life on the road
summary: One has to move to New York to work out of it; he is now mostly touring.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: What is the state of jazz in New York for you right now? Does it seem pretty healthy?
Well you know a friend of mine said something that was very true. You have to move to New York to work out of New York.
Once you get there you find yourself going somewhere.

Exactly. So in the last few years now I’ve been pretty much road running, which is great I mean that’s what I’ve always wanted to do my whole life and I thank God for it. But you know usually when I’m in New York these days, when I’m home I’m doing a few recording sessions or you know just catching up on bills or all of that fun stuff.
